# Which settings mattered (auto-generated by core_settings.py)

A setting counts as having **mattered** in a task when its effect is real (paired z > 3) and big enough to care about: accuracy moves 2+ points, or thought time moves 15%+ of baseline, or neuron count moves 25%+ of baseline. Four task conditions (medium/hard x shift/replace), 24 repeats each.

| Setting | Mattered in | What moved | Beat the start value? | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rho | 4/4 tasks | acc: 0.638 to 0.993 (z 88); t: 19.4 to 183 (z 37) | yes | **candidate**: Matters and some value beat the start: next question is whether the best value DEPENDS ON THE WORLD (if so, the brain should adjust it itself). |
| select | 4/4 tasks | n: 11.3 to 14.5 (z 9) | yes | **candidate**: Matters and some value beat the start: next question is whether the best value DEPENDS ON THE WORLD (if so, the brain should adjust it itself). |

| eta | 4/4 tasks | t: 31 to 47.9 (z 10) | no | **builtin**: Matters, but the start value (0.5) is already the best in every task: fix it as a constant. |
